microtheory.name: ecological_psychology_perception
microtheory.definition: Gibson's ecological approach to perception. Direct perception of affordances. Information specifies perceiver-environment relations. Rejects representationalism. Substrate analogue: substrate's direct-affordance approach to inputs.

concepts.name: direct_perception
concepts.definition: Gibson. Perception not constructed from impoverished input via inference. Information specifies environment directly. Substrate analogue: substrate's direct-input interpretation.

concepts.name: rich_stimulus
concepts.definition: Gibson. Environment provides ample information for perception when correctly analyzed. Substrate analogue: substrate's information-rich input.

concepts.name: ambient_array
concepts.definition: Optic, acoustic, etc. Structured arrays of energy reaching perceiver. Substrate analogue: substrate's full-input field.

concepts.name: optic_array_gibson
concepts.definition: Structured light from environment. Constrained by 3D world. Substrate analogue: substrate's structured visual input.

concepts.name: invariant_information
concepts.definition: Properties of stimulus array constant under transformation (e.g., self-motion). Specify environmental features. Substrate analogue: substrate's transformation-invariant features.

concepts.name: transformational_invariant
concepts.definition: What persists across changes. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin-stable properties.

concepts.name: affordance_concept
concepts.definition: Gibson 1979. Action possibilities for animal in environment. Relational property. Substrate analogue: substrate's environment-action coupling.

concepts.name: graspability
concepts.definition: Affordance for grasping. Specified by handle size relative to hand. Substrate analogue: substrate's action-capability matching.

concepts.name: walkability
concepts.definition: Affordance for walking. Surface flatness, friction, gap size relative to step. Substrate analogue: substrate's traversability.

concepts.name: reachability
concepts.definition: Affordance for reaching. Distance relative to arm length. Substrate analogue: substrate's range-of-action.

concepts.name: affordance_perception
concepts.definition: Affordances perceived directly, not inferred from features. Substrate analogue: substrate's direct-action-availability.

concepts.name: tau_function
concepts.definition: Lee 1976. Time-to-contact from optical expansion rate. Used in steering + collision avoidance. Substrate analogue: substrate's temporal-margin computation.

concepts.name: optical_flow
concepts.definition: Pattern of motion in optic array. Specifies self-motion + scene structure + heading. Substrate analogue: substrate's flow-from-action.

concepts.name: focus_of_expansion_ecological
concepts.definition: Point in optic flow that doesn't move during locomotion. Heading direction. Substrate analogue: substrate's action-direction marker.

concepts.name: perception_action_cycle_gibson
concepts.definition: Continuous loop of perception → action → new perception. No discrete steps. Substrate analogue: substrate's continuous loop.

concepts.name: active_exploration
concepts.definition: Perception requires + drives exploration. Movement generates new information. Substrate analogue: substrate's exploration-based learning.

concepts.name: perception_as_information_pickup
concepts.definition: Not construction — picking up what's already there. Substrate analogue: substrate's affordance-detection.

concepts.name: ecological_optics
concepts.definition: Gibson. Optics of perceiver-environment system. Substrate analogue: substrate's perceiver-environment coupling theory.

concepts.name: texture_gradient
concepts.definition: Surface texture density varies with distance + slant. Cue to depth + orientation. Substrate analogue: substrate's spatial-feature cue.

concepts.name: horizon_ratio
concepts.definition: Same-height objects intersect horizon at same fraction. Invariant for size. Substrate analogue: substrate's reference-invariant.

concepts.name: ecological_validity
concepts.definition: Brunswik. Cue's correlation with environmental property. Useful info has high ecological validity. Substrate analogue: substrate's reliable-feature criterion.

concepts.name: brunswik_lens_model
concepts.definition: Brunswik. Probabilistic relations between distal property, proximal cues, perceiver inference. Substrate analogue: substrate's inferential cue-utilization.

concepts.name: infant_perception_ecological
concepts.definition: Babies use ecological information from birth. Visual cliff (Walk + Gibson 1961). Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded ecological priors.

concepts.name: visual_cliff_experiment
concepts.definition: Walk + Gibson 1961. Infants refuse to crawl over apparent drop. Direct depth perception. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded-danger detection.

concepts.name: ecological_realism
concepts.definition: Environment exists independently + provides perceivable information about itself. Substrate analogue: substrate's grounded-environment view.

concepts.name: anti_representationalism_gibson
concepts.definition: Gibson + ecological psychology reject internal representations as theoretical entities. Information IN the environment. Substrate analogue: substrate's direct-information view.

rules.name: perception_is_direct_information_pickup
rules.head: the substrate receives structured input
rules.body: the input contains information specifying environmental features directly — perception picks it up, doesn't reconstruct. Gibson. Substrate's direct perception.

rules.name: affordances_couple_environment_to_action
rules.head: the substrate perceives an environment
rules.body: affordances specify available actions given substrate's capabilities. Substrate's coupled action-perception.

rules.name: movement_generates_invariants_for_pickup
rules.head: the substrate moves through environment
rules.body: optical flow + transformation invariants emerge that specify both self-motion + environment. Substrate's exploration-generates-info.

rules.name: tau_specifies_time_to_contact
rules.head: the substrate approaches an object
rules.body: the inverse rate of optical expansion specifies time-to-contact. Lee 1976. Substrate's temporal-margin estimation.

rules.name: ecological_validity_filters_useful_cues
rules.head: the substrate uses environmental cues for inference
rules.body: high-validity cues (those reliably correlated with environmental properties) are most useful. Brunswik. Substrate's reliable-cue prioritization.
